summary:
The Meskwaki Nation is a self-governing nation on the Meskwaki Settlement in Tama County, Iowa. Its federal name is the Sac and Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa, but the people have always called themselves Meskwaki, the Red Earth People. "Fox" came from the French. "Sac and Fox" came from an 1804 treaty that wrongly treated the Meskwaki and Sauk as one tribe.

Treaties in the 1840s took the Meskwaki's Iowa lands and sent the people to a reservation in Kansas. Some never left, and others came back. In 1856 Iowa passed a law letting them stay, and on July 13, 1857, the Meskwaki bought 80 acres of their own in Tama County. Because the people bought it themselves, the Settlement is privately owned land held in common. It is not a reservation. It now covers more than 8,000 acres, and July 13 is a Meskwaki national holiday.

When the government tried to force Meskwaki children into boarding school, parents went to court. Since the 1980s the Nation has run its own school, centered on Meskwaki language and culture. In World War II, eight Meskwaki men served as code talkers in North Africa.

notes: Word count is about 195. The 1857 purchase is confirmed by three sources. meskwaki.org, SHSI and Iowa PBS all give July 13, 1857, and 80 acres. The 1856 Iowa law has three sources (meskwaki.org, Iowa PBS and OHS). For the 1840s removal, meskwaki.org gives 1845 and Iowa PBS gives an 1842 treaty with a deadline of 1845, so only the decade is used. 'More than 8,000 acres' is backed by meskwaki.org (8,100+) and Iowa PBS (8,000+). The code talker facts (eight men, North Africa, WWII) are backed by NMAI and the Iowa Senate resolution. LEFT OUT: (1) The 1857 price (about $1,000). Only Iowa PBS gives it. (2) The 1867 purchase of 40 acres paid for with 130 trees. Only meskwaki.org gives it. (3) The 1896 transfer of trusteeship from Iowa to the federal government. Only Iowa PBS gives it. (4) The Toledo Boarding School dates, 1898–1910. Only Iowa PBS gives them. (5) The year the Nation took over its school. SHSI says 1980 and Iowa PBS says 1981, so the draft uses 'since the 1980s'. (6) 'Only federally recognized tribe in Iowa.' Only meskwaki.org says it, and it is a superlative. The 'went to court' sentence rests on Iowa PBS alone. Placing the Settlement on the Iowa River also rests on Iowa PBS alone, so it was dropped.
